carousels.name: 5 phone settings that make relapse harder

slides.title: 5 phone settings that make relapse [[way harder.]]
slides.sub: Your phone is set up for the habit by default. Change that.

slides.title: Settings [[1–2]]
items: Turn on content restrictions in Screen Time (iPhone) or Digital Wellbeing (Android).
Let someone else set the passcode so you can't switch it off at 1 AM.

slides.title: Settings [[3–4]]
items: Set app limits on the apps you scroll late at night.
Turn on grayscale after 10 PM — a dull screen is far less tempting.

slides.title: Use [[Bedtime]] mode
slides.body: Schedule Sleep or Bedtime mode so notifications and apps go quiet at night. The phone tells you when it's time to stop — not the other way around.

slides.title: Friction [[wins.]]
slides.body: Every extra step between you and the habit is a moment to choose differently. Set it up once, while you're strong.

carousels.name: Ambushed by a trigger: the 3-second rule

slides.kicker: When it comes out of nowhere
slides.title: A scene. An ad. A post. [[Use the 3-second rule.]]
slides.sub: What to do when a trigger ambushes you.

slides.title: Look [[away]]
slides.body: The first glance isn't your fault. The second look is a choice. Eyes off the screen within 3 seconds.

slides.title: Name [[it]]
slides.body: Say it in your head: "That's a trigger." Labeling it puts you back in control, instead of on autopilot.

slides.title: Do something [[physical]]
slides.body: Stand up. Walk to another room. Splash water on your face. A body in motion breaks the spell.

slides.title: Prevent the [[next]] ambush
items: Skip the scene or switch shows — no shame in it.
slides.note: Where do triggers ambush you most? Comment it 👇

slides.title:
Three seconds.
[[Then a plan.]]
slides.lead: Hit the panic button for instant tools the moment a trigger hits, and journal it to spot the pattern.

carousels.name: Your why has to be bigger than the urge

slides.title: If your "why" is weak, [[the urge will win.]]
slides.sub: The reason you're quitting needs to be bigger than the moment.

slides.title: "Because I [[should]]" isn't enough
slides.body: Vague reasons collapse at 1 AM. You need something that actually matters to you.

slides.title: Make it [[personal]]
slides.body: The partner you want to be present for. The confidence you want back. The man you want to become. Specific beats general.

slides.title: Keep it [[visible]]
slides.body:
A reason you can't see is a reason you'll forget.

Put it on your lock screen, your mirror, your journal's first page.

slides.title: Write your [[why]]
items: Add who it's for — you, a partner, your future self.
Write what you'll gain, not just what you'll lose.
slides.note: Share your why in one sentence. It might help someone else 👇

slides.title:
Remember why
[[you started.]]
slides.lead: Journal your reasons, track your progress and get support when your why feels far away.

carousels.name: 23 days left in November: learn a skill

slides.title: Don't just avoid it this month. [[Build something.]]
slides.sub: Turn the rest of November into a skill you'll keep.

slides.title: Avoiding isn't [[enough]]
slides.body: "Don't do it" leaves an empty space. A new skill gives your evenings something to say yes to.

slides.title: Pick [[one]] thing
slides.body: Guitar. Cooking. Coding. A language. Drawing. Training for a run. One skill, 20 minutes a day, for the rest of the month.

slides.title: Do it at your [[danger hour]]
slides.body: Schedule practice for the time urges usually hit. Your hardest hour becomes your growth hour.

slides.title: Make it [[stick]]
slides.note: What skill are you learning this month? Comment it — we'll check in 👇

Quit the habit.

slides.lead: Daily actions, habit tracking and streaks to keep both going all month.

carousels.name: How to help a friend who's struggling

slides.kicker: Send this to your group chat
slides.title: Your friend might be [[fighting this in silence.]]
slides.sub: How to help without making it weird.

slides.title: It's more [[common]] than you think
slides.body: Plenty of guys struggle with this and never mention it. Your friend might be one of them — and waiting for someone to make it safe to talk.

slides.title: Go [[first]]
slides.body: Share something real about your own struggles, whatever they are. Openness invites openness.

slides.title: Don't [[judge]] or joke
slides.body: If he opens up, don't laugh it off or lecture. Say: "Respect for telling me. How can I help?"

slides.title: Ways to [[help]]
items: Check in without making it a big deal.
Point him to tools and support, not shame.
slides.note: Tag a friend you'd always have the back of 👇

slides.title:
Quit together.
[[Win together.]]
slides.lead: 1-on-1 accountability, public habit tracking a friend can see and an anonymous community.
